additions.reason: The Torah text explicitly equates עֹנִי (poverty/lack) as a bechina of מלכות. 'מַלְכוּת הוּא בְּחִינַת עֹנִי וְהַכְנָעָה' — Kingship is an aspect of poverty and submission. This is explained through the principle 'אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּלֹא עָם': Malkhut has nothing of its own (לית לה מגרמה כלום), making it structurally identical to poverty — a state of having nothing independently. עֹנִי is not the cause of Malkhut; they share the same essential nature of self-emptiness and dependence. This node belongs in Package 2 alongside מלכות and הכנעה.
additions.source_quote: וּמַלְכוּת הוּא בְּחִינַת עֹנִי וְהַכְנָעָה, כִּי אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּלֹא עָם

additions.reason: The Torah text calls the act of God asking ('שׁוֹאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ') a bechina of hakhna'ah and shiplut. 'כִּי שׁוֹאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ, הוּא בְּחִינַת הַכְנָעָה וְשִׁפְלוּת, כְּמוֹ הַשּׁוֹאֵל וּמְבַקֵּשׁ מֵחֲבֵרוֹ' — the one who asks from another is structurally in a position of submission. God 'asking' Israel to accept His Kingship is therefore not a causal act but an expression of His self-diminishment (tzimtzum of gaavah), making it bechina-identical to hakhna'ah. This node belongs in Package 2, as it is another facet of the same essential quality of self-lowering that defines מלכות-יראה-הכנעה.

additions.reason: The Torah text (line 10) on the verse 'אִם יִסָּתֵר אִישׁ בְּמִסְתָּרִים' interprets hiding/concealment as bechina of humility and self-nullification. The hiding of oneself in misatarim is equated with the same self-erasure that is ענוה ושפלות. The text says 'שֶׁמַּסְתִּיר וּמַעֲלִים וּמַקְטִין אֶת עַצְמוֹ בַּעֲנָוָה וְשִׁפְלוּת' — hiding/concealing oneself IS the act of humility. This makes הסתרה (self-concealment) a bechina of ענוה ושפלות, placing it in Package 1. Note: the same concept applies to God's self-concealment (tzimtzum of gaavah), making this a bridging concept between the two packages — but since it is framed in the passage as an expression of ענוה, Package 1 is the primary assignment.

analysis_notes.structural_note: The two packages in Torah #219 are thematically very close — both describe self-nullification. Package 1 (אין/לא/ענוה ושפלות) focuses on the ontological and linguistic dimension of nothingness; Package 2 (מלכות/יראה/הכנעה) focuses on the relational and structural dimension of Kingship as self-emptying. The Torah text strongly suggests these two clusters share the same essential quality (both are aspects of God's tzimtzum/self-smallening), but since there is no bechina edge directly connecting a node from Package 1 to a node from Package 2 in the dataset, they are kept as two separate connected components. A candidate bridge edge would be: ענוה ושפלות ↔ הכנעה (both are the same quality named differently), or אין ↔ עוני (nothingness and poverty are the same lack-of-independent-substance). These are strong candidates for new edges to add to the dataset.
analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror: Torah #219 presents only the positive dimension of self-nullification. The negative counterpart (גאוה / pride / self-aggrandizement) is discussed extensively as the force that destroys the Temple, but it is not given any bechina nodes — it functions as the eitza-antagonist.
